thread:
incident-bot: @oncall HIGH severity alert: serving-runtime-gpu-pool producing repeated CUDA OOMs and container crashloops across autoscaled nodes. Error rate spiked 3.2x in last 5m, 5xxs and timeouts for generation endpoints. Paging SRE.

Sara K.: ack, I'm on it. starting investigation — grabbing logs from the affected pool.

Mike L.: oncall here, adding context: this started right after the autoscaler change that lowered scaleDownStabilization from 5m -> 20s this morning. possible rapid scale down/up thrash.

Laura M.: seeing repeated: `CUDA out of memory` in ai-runtime logs, then kubelet restart loops on nodes. sample:
```
E tensorflow: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
W serving: failed to allocate kv_cache (size=1.2GB)
container "runtime" exited code=137, signal=9
```

James R.: also noticing node memory usage jumps right before crash, but GPU mem stays high for a single pod for a while, then crash. suspect bad packing/oversubscription during scale events.

Sara K.: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable aggressive scale-down (set min replicas = current replicas for 10m) 2) cordon most noisy nodes 3) enable model-fallback to smaller-quant variant for high-latency routes 4) open customer comms draft. applying changes now.

Dave P.: +1. I'm running `kubectl patch hpa/serving-pool --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'` to prevent scale down while we stabilize.

Laura M.: cordoning node gpu-prod-17 (list shows 4 crashloops there). running: `kubectl drain gpu-prod-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

Mike L.: temporarily toggled autoscaler cooldown: `scaleDownStabilizationSeconds=600` and `scaleDownUnneededTime=600`. will watch for thrash.

Sara K.: enabling prefix caching ring for long-tail customers to reduce kv cache pressure. asking infra to pause new deploys to serving runtime.

incident-bot: Deploy freeze enabled on namespace: serving-prod by Sara K.

James R.: I pushed a conservative scheduler patch to prefer spreading heavy pods across nodes instead of binpack. This should reduce single-pod GPU saturation. Monitoring.

Laura M.: Observation: traffic burst pattern correlated with scheduled nightly batch fanout at 14:00 UTC — that triggered autoscaler to spin down earlier and then a sudden fanout later. Suggest adding rate-limiter at ingress for that job.

Sara K.: Customer impact assessment: approx 12% of hosted text-generation requests retuning 5xx in last 10m, latency >2s for another 20%. Dedicated contracts unaffected. Opening support ticket list: TKT-5021, TKT-5022. Notifying prioritized customers.

support-bot: Support note template ready: "We are investigating intermittent 5xxs affecting a subset of hosted inference requests. Mitigations are in progress; next update in 30 minutes."

Mike L.: After minReplicas bump and cordon/drain, crashloops decreased from 18 nodes -> 4 nodes in 8m. CPU stable, GPU memory pressure still high on two problematic pods.

Sara K.: rolling restart of runtime on the two pods with mismatched kv_cache allocation (manually delete pod to reprovision). executed `kubectl delete pod runtime-abc-2` -> new pod came up healthy.

Laura M.: adding temporary auto-fallback route: requests > 8s go to `model-quant-small` until we finish root cause. Config pushed.

James R.: root cause hypothesis: autoscaler rapid scale down during low traffic removed nodes holding warm KV caches. When traffic spiked, many new pods tried to rebuild kv_cache simultaneously, triggering high GPU allocation and OOMs. The quick scale-up created packing conflicts and contention.

Dave P.: long-term fix ideas: 1) warm standby nodes / cache warmers, 2) add staggered pod startup/KV-cache backoff, 3) autoscaler soft-evict with dampening per pool.

Mike L.: for now: keep minReplicas locked for 30m, maintain deploy freeze, continue draining the flappy nodes, and plan a canary for the scheduler change.

Sara K.: drafting customer message for urgent-affected list. CC: support and eng-ops.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty handoff in 45m to Oncall-L2. Handoff checklist: mitigation steps, current config, support tickets, logs (links posted in thread).

Laura M.: posting links to logs and dashboards: https://redwood-infra/logs/serving-pool?since=15m and https://redwood-monitor/prod/serving/gpu-pool.

Mike L.: preparing post-incident action items: update autoscaler safety defaults, add startup backoff to runtime, implement cache prefetch for critical models, add alert for simultaneous high allocation across >40% of pool.

Sara K.: agreed. final note before handoff: system looks more stable after conservative changes, error rate down to 1.3x baseline. will hand off to Mike L. (L2) in 35m.

Mike L.: taking over. Sara — can you paste the exact `kubectl` commands you ran for minReplicas and scheduler patch so I can reproduce if needed?

Sara K.: paste -
```bash
kubectl patch hpa/serving-pool -n serving-prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'
kubectl label node gpu-prod-17 cordoned=true
kubectl drain gpu-prod-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# scheduler patch: rollout restart deployment/serving-scheduler -n serving-prod
```

Mike L.: got it. thanks. I'll keep thread updated and coordinate customer comms with Support.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation active, degradations reduced, customers notified. Severity: P2 -> monitor. Next update in 30m or on any regressions.

Dave P.: postmortem owners volunteered: Sara K. (runbook/update autoscaler), James R. (scheduler/pack policy), Laura M. (cache backoff), Mike L. (oncall followup + customer comms).

Laura M.: quick note — don't forget to add test harness for burst+scale test in staging to avoid re-introducing this.

Mike L.: handing over to next oncall: @James R. will be triage lead for the night if anything flares up.

James R.: standing by.

Sara K.: thanks team. closing my active tasks and marking deploy freeze until 2026-03-16T10:00:00Z (UTC) unless we opt-out earlier.

support-bot: Internal support notice sent to affected customers and CS channels.

incident-bot: thread locked for edits. Use follow-up channels for new actions.
